newsitem.title: FINLAND: VATTENFALL BIDS FOR FINNISH SAVON VOIMA -PAPER.
newsitem.headline: VATTENFALL BIDS FOR FINNISH SAVON VOIMA -PAPER.

text.p: Swedish state-owned power producer Vattenfall AB has offered to buy the entire share capital of Finnish regional power company Savon Voima for 807 million markka, daily Helsingin Sanomat said on Tuesday.
"Savon Voima's 30 owner-municipalities and corporations have until the middle of June to consider their answer to Vattenfall," the newspaper said.
Savon Voima has annual net sales of over 560 million markka, and is mainly owned by the municipalities of the Kuopio area in east-central Finland, the paper said.
Vattenfall's Finnish subsidiary Vattenfall Oy already owns two other regional power companies in Finland: Hameen Sahko Oy and Lapuan Sahko Oy, the paper said.
Vattenfall has also been in talks with the owners of two other Finnish regional power groups, Keski-Suomen Valo and Suur-Savon Sahko, it said.

"One of these three companies would be enough for us at this stage, and we managed to get down to positive talks with Savon Voima," the paper quoted Vattenfall Oy's chief executive Kaj Hagglund as saying.
Vattenfall's offer would mean a price of 1,400 markka per Savon Voima share, the newspaper said.
Vattenfall wants to acquire at least half of the Savon Voima share capital and votes, Helsingin Sanomat said.
